status: Illustrative unbuilt retail garden concepts. No surveyed site, engineering validation, exact-model rendering, observed plant growth or completed installation is asserted.

images.prompt:
Use case: architectural concept visualisation / precise object integration.
Create a new 16:9 architectural presentation hero for Bower in a contemporary UK outdoor shopping-centre square. Reference 1 is the previous concept: retain its credible modern pale-stone retail frontages, glass shops and human scale, but replace its weak, isolated landscape composition. Reference 2 is the authoritative GEOMETRY: ONE six-bay timber pavilion shown from three viewpoints, not three structures. Preserve the pointed timber arches, six supports, open circular crown and fine interwoven roof lattice. Reference 3 supplies the trained climber foliage character, not a location.

The pavilion must be the centre of a complete, exceptionally well-designed retail GARDEN, not an object placed on empty paving. Substantial connected planting beds extend far beyond its footprint into the foreground and toward a café terrace, echoing the structure's circular geometry in a coherent landscape plan. Low pale-stone planter walls with integrated warm timber sitting edges; generous richly layered groundcover, perennials, soft grasses, evergreen shrubs and a few small multi-stem trees at the perimeter. Restrained white and muted purple seasonal flowers. Repeat the same materials and plant palette throughout. Climbers emerge from generous real soil beds beside the supports, their timber base connections remain clear of soil and visually accessible. Fuller but believable trained leaf cover, leaving the timber form and open crown visible. Ground-level planted areas mixed with low raised beds, not a halo of disconnected pots. A few simple integrated seats under the canopy instead of the dominant central circular bench.

Make the landscape read as a single inviting outdoor room tied to adjacent shops. Keep generous level paths through the planting and around the edges, three readable approach routes, visible entrances and unobstructed storefront sightlines. Include ordinary shoppers walking, a few people resting beside planting, and café tables at the edge. One pavilion at small-room scale, not a giant plaza canopy. The immediate setting should be predominantly designed garden and useful paths, not a broad vacant paved field.

Composition: broad view at ordinary eye level; the pavilion occupies middle/right, wholly visible including bases; lush layered planted edges sweep from the foreground toward it. Left quarter may be calmer planting/shadow for a short title, but do not waste half the image on blank paving. Shops remain clearly identifiable behind and beside the garden. Natural bright overcast UK light, premium realistic architectural photography, believable materials and careful planting detail. No country house, palace, lawns, woodland, fantasy tunnel, repeated pavilion, fountains, crowds or oversized trees. No text, logos, captions, watermarks or legible brand names. This is an illustrative unbuilt design, not a documentary installation photograph.
referenceRoles: retail-square.png: retail setting and scale, replace landscape composition

images.prompt:
Use case: architectural concept visualisation, same-design second camera view.
Create a second 16:9 image of exactly the same illustrated Bower RETAIL GARDEN as reference 1. Reference 2 is authoritative pavilion geometry: one six-bay timber pavilion shown from three viewpoints, with pointed arches, fine interwoven lattice and open circular crown. Preserve the garden identity established in reference 1: contemporary pale-stone and glass shopping-centre façades, curving low pale-stone planting walls, warm timber sitting edges, generous connected planting beds with layered perennials, grasses, shrubs, muted purple and white flowers and small multi-stem trees; climbers trained onto the timber pavilion.

Move the camera close to seated eye level at the edge of a planting bed, looking obliquely through one pavilion opening towards shops and the café beyond. It should feel like sitting in a deliberately designed garden within a working retail centre. Foreground low flowers and grasses frame a comfortable timber seating edge; two or three ordinary visitors sit and talk at middle/right, one person rests with shopping bags; passing shoppers visible beyond. The actual pointed timber arches and woven roof overhead remain identifiable, with believable partial trained foliage. Show substantial soil beds beside supports and visible accessible timber bases. Preserve the same material language and planting species as reference 1, not a new setting. Clear level paths through the garden, visible shop entrances, a few café tables. Do not insert a large isolated doughnut bench or replace the garden with empty paving. Do not overwhelm the small pavilion with enormous trees or densely block retail sightlines.

Keep the left quarter quieter/darker for a short slide title while the interesting seated experience occupies the centre/right. Natural bright lightly overcast UK daylight matching reference 1, realistic human-scale architectural photography, refined materials and believable plants. No country house, lawn, woodland, repeated pavilion, giant canopy, water feature, exaggerated flowers, readable signs, logos, captions or watermark. Illustrative unbuilt concept, not a documentary project photograph.
